newsitem.title: USA: Florida Power seeks to recover fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: Florida Power seeks to recover fuel costs.

text.p: Florida Power Corp on Tuesday said it was seeking an increase in the fuel-expense portion of customer bills, due to an extended maintenance outage at the Crystal River nuclear plant.
The average 1,000-kilowatt-hour bill for residential customers would increase to $88.65 from $83.39, effective April 1, the company said.
The increase is subject to approval by the Florida Public Service Commission.
The additional fuel charge would cover the cost of power to compensate for the nuclear plant being out of service, Florida Power said. It also reflected higher oil and natural gas prices, it said.
Florida Power said fuel expense charges were a direct pass-through item on customers bills, so it would not earn any profit on the increase.
The company said its replacement power fuel costs were about $10 million a month.
The 860-megawatt unit, shut down in September, is undergoing an extensive upgrade.
Florida Power shares dipped 1/4 to 25-1/2 in trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
